implementationPlan.description:
Phase 2 (CRITICAL DESIGN FINDING - read before writing any code) - THE TWO WRITER PATHS NEED DIFFERENT SUBJECT SOURCES, and the row description's single phrase "subjectRef/subjectRevision come server-side from the active graph binding" hides it.
The reader joins at `policy-risk-reader.ts:124-130`: `active = readCurrentActiveGraph(store, projectId)`, then `record.subjectRef === active.graphContentHash` and `record.subjectRevision === active.graphEpoch`. A revision is ACTIVE only when its own aggregate replays to `lifecycle === "ACTIVE"` (`active-graph-projection.ts:156-176`). The two paths diverge:
(A) `graph.approve` -> `graph-activation-service.ts:214-217` ALWAYS carries `transition.leg` - the revision-activation leg - in `extraLegs`, so THAT COMMIT IS WHAT MAKES THE REVISION ACTIVE. Calling `readCurrentActiveGraph` there returns the PREVIOUS revision (or ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT on genesis), so a record written from it would be STALE THE INSTANT IT COMMITS and the reader would reject it forever - a dead record, written successfully, that no test asserting "a record was written" would catch.
CORRECTED OPERAND (d950bd95 amend-1, confirmed by worker-4aba1617 comment-2426748e and re-measured at 7177c0a6): take BOTH values from `transition.state`, not `transition.binding`. `GraphActivationBinding` (packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts) is exactly {budgetHash, expectedGoalVersion, graphHash, policyHash, qualityHash} and has NO graphEpoch. `GraphTransitionAccepted` (apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-transition-legs.ts:46-51) returns {binding, leg, ok, state}, and `GraphRevisionState` carries BOTH `graphContentHash` (:125) and `graphEpoch` (:132). So: `subjectRef = transition.state.graphContentHash`; `subjectRevision = transition.state.graphEpoch`. Those are the SAME FIELD NAMES the reader compares against, so there is no cross-field mapping to get wrong. `graphEpoch`'s docstring: ">= 1 exactly when the lifecycle is ACTIVE or SUPERSEDED, and exactly 0 otherwise" - after the activation leg it is the activated epoch the reader will observe: assert it is >= 1 in the qualifying-approval arm, and treat a 0 epoch as a refusal to emit the leg rather than writing a record the reader can never match.
(B) `approval.decide` -> `approval-activation.ts` builds NO revision-activation leg (its only extra is the budget root), so it does not move the active graph and `readCurrentActiveGraph(store, request.projectId)` IS the correct subject source there.
DELIVERABLE OF THIS STEP: no production edit - confirm both halves on disk at your HEAD and record the exact expression you will use for subjectRef/subjectRevision on EACH path in a durable comment. If `transition.state` does not expose both fields at your HEAD, STOP and report blocked naming the missing field: writing the wrong subject is worse than not writing.
